description: Column MASKING policies and ROW ACCESS policies: creating them, attaching them, the values they produce, and the roles that bypass them. A masking policy is created with its signature and body and attaches to a COLUMN; an administrative role (SYSADMIN, ACCOUNTADMIN) sees the RAW value while an ordinary role sees the masked one. The masking is applied to the COLUMN REFERENCE rather than to the output, which is the regression the middle group pins: any expression around the column used to leak the raw data, so the masked value is asserted inside a function call, a concatenation, arithmetic and a qualified reference, while a STRING LITERAL that merely happens to spell the column's name is NOT rewritten and an unmasked column in the same SELECT is untouched. Policies can be dropped, replaced, renamed (both spellings), renamed with IF EXISTS as a silent no-op, and a rename of a missing policy throws. Two TAG-DRIVEN policies key off SYSTEM and SYSTEM, so the same policy masks one column and leaves another alone. Row access policies filter ROWS by the same role logic, can block everything, detach from the table, drop as objects and rename. The last test runs both kinds at once. Converted 1:1 from security/PolicyEnforcementTest (now retired); the Java read the catalog directly for every existence and attachment claim, which becomes SHOW MASKING POLICIES / SHOW ROW ACCESS POLICIES LIKE for existence, DESCRIBE MASKING POLICY for the signature and body, and TABLE(INFORMATION_SCHEMA.POLICY_REFERENCES(...)) for the attachments - and its setCurrentRole calls become plain USE ROLE.
